Versus
 State Of U.P. & Anr. Respondent
O R D E R
1. Leave granted.

2.  We have heard the learned counsel appearing for the appellant and the learned counsel appearing for the respondents, i.e., the State and the Complainant.
3.

The appellant has been arrayed as an accused in Crime No. 98 of 2024, registered with Police Station- Bihar, District- Unnao for the offences punishable under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471,
120-B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
4. The fact remains that investigation is complete and the charge-sheet has already been filed.
5. Though non-bailable warrant has been issued against the appellant, the only issue that remains for consideration is the co- operation of the appellant.
6. Learned counsel appearing for the appellant submits that the appellant could not appear before the Trial Court as he was apprehending his arrest.
7. Considering the above, we are inclined to set aside the impugned order and grant anticipatory bail to the appellant.

8. Accordingly, the impugned order stands set aside and the appellant is granted anticipatory bail,
subject to the terms and conditions to the satisfaction of the Trial Court.
The Trial Court shall additionally impose a condition to the effect that the appellant shall co-operate with the conduct of the trial.
